description: Figure 5 presents the relationship between the effectiveness of Enhanced GCG and the number of samples used across various downstream tasks. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of samples,” displays categories representing sample sizes: 1, 3, 5, 10, and 50. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy,” represents values ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with a linear scale and tick marks at 0.1 intervals. Four colored lines represent different tasks: MCQ Union, LMQ Reform, Corpora Union, and Corpora Reform. The line for MCQ Union starts at approximately 0.15 for 1 sample, rises to approximately 0.3 for 3 samples, plateaus around 0.35 for 5, 10, and 50 samples. The LMQ Reform line begins at approximately 0.1 for 1 sample, increases to approximately 0.2 for 3 samples, and then rises to approximately 0.4 for 5 samples, before leveling off around 0.45 for 10 and 50 samples. The Corpora Union line starts at approximately 0.3 for 1 sample, increases to approximately 0.4 for 3 samples, and then rises to approximately 0.5 for 5 samples, before leveling off around 0.5 for 10 and 50 samples. Finally, the Corpora Reform line begins at approximately 0.2 for 1 sample, increases to approximately 0.3 for 3 samples, and then rises to approximately 0.4 for 5 samples, before leveling off around 0.45 for 10 and 50 samples. The lines are not explicitly sorted, and no bars or lines are visually emphasized.
